key_insight: AegisDx reframes AI diagnosis from a single prediction into a safety-oriented reasoning workflow that broadens differential diagnosis, checks for dangerous misses, and verifies evidence-backed reasoning.
clinical_relevance: This could improve bedside decision support in acute care by making AI outputs more transparent, more safety-focused, and less likely to overlook must-not-miss conditions.
method: Uses role-specific LLM components with structured intermediate outputs and verification gates.
Adds evidence-retrieval interfaces to ground reasoning in medical literature.
Explicitly screens for high-risk must-not-miss diagnoses before finalizing recommendations.
evidence_signal: Across literature cases and emergency-department notes, AegisDx improved Top-3 diagnostic performance and safety metrics versus standalone LLM baselines, including a physician-rated composite safety score gain from 4.31 to 4.55.
watch_item: Performance depends on the underlying model, retrieval quality, and workflow integration, so real-world safety gains still need broader external validation before routine deployment.
paper_title: A safety-oriented hypothetico-deductive framework for AI-assisted differential diagnosis
